doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Homes in East Hampton and New York, liking Italy, and not sightseeing
summary: He splits time between New York and East Hampton, says he would like a place in Italy, and only wants to travel to work.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: So you say you have a house in the East Hampton?
Yeah.
So you divide your time between here and Manhattan and East Hampton.
Yes.
Do you have any other abodes? Do you still have a place in Los Angeles?
I had a dynamite place in L.A. I gave it to my son. I had a dynamite place in L.A. I think if I was able to get another place it would probably be in Italy.
Why Italy?
Why not?
Okay.
I like Italy man. Italy has soulful people, man. Have you ever been over there?
Oh yeah.
Soulful man. I prefer Italy to France, you know. They are just soulful, man. Plus the fact they dig me and I dig them.
They love jazz. They know. They are in tune.
They made a wine for me, you know.
We need to get more of this information. Where is that winery?
What the hell was it -­
Was it northern?
I don’t know they were so many all over that place.
And you are a world traveler, is there any place in the world that you have not been that you would like travel to?

Not necessarily, which is really strange because my brother, my younger brother Don, this dude goes all over the world for jazz concerts. He is going to Australia in a couple of weeks. He takes the tours, him and his wife. That is all they do. He can afford it so that is all they do. But at this stage of the game man, you know the only time I want to go someplace is if I am working. I have never been interested in historical events or that kind of thing. You know I go there to play, do my gig and get out of dodge. I have always been -- I don’t know maybe I should take a little time to smell the roses but that is not what I am all about.
